key_insight: An NLP ensemble combining radiology Findings and Impressions identified brain metastases more sensitively than either section alone.
clinical_relevance: The pipeline could expand cancer registry surveillance to brain metastases developing after the initial cancer diagnosis; it is not a drug discovery tool.
method: Manually labeled brain/head radiology reports from an Alberta cancer cohort diagnosed in 2012–2019.
Trained separate Bio_ClinicalBERT models for Findings and Impressions, using the higher probability as the report-level prediction.
Validated internally in Alberta and externally in Ontario and British Columbia.
evidence_signal: Trained on 1,879 samples, the ensemble achieved 88.8% sensitivity and 49.9% precision on 1,833 internal-validation reports at a 0.4 threshold; external sensitivity was 91.8% in Ontario and 72.6% in British Columbia.
watch_item: Modest internal precision and variable external sensitivity warrant local validation and review workflows before registry implementation.
paper_title: Natural Language Processing Based Solution for Labeling Brain Metastasis Identified in Radiology Reports
